text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Head of State, General Sani Abacha, orders importation of fuel and immediate supply of petrol to Lagos.

- Central bank orders investigation into foreign exchange allocations at its weekly auctions. A central bank statement said that banks which are unable to back up their requests and show where foreign exchange has gone will face sanctions.
- Fresh protests rock the southern oil city of Warri as people demonstrate against annulment of a local government election.
- Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund has invested 3.5 billion naira in blue chip equities and government treasury bills, the funds managing director says.

- United Nations human rights rapporteurs revealed an unflattering list of Nigerian rights violations at a session of the U.N. Commission on Human Rights in Geneva on Tuesday. The rapporteurs called on the military government to abolish draconian decrees and release political prisoners.

- Nigeria's reluctance to merge dual exchange rates and to privatise major state-owned bodies have been identified in a paper by finance minister, Anthony Ani, as obstacles to the agreement of a formal Medium Term Economic Strategy with international lending institutions.
- Sam Aluko, chairman of the National Economic Intelligence Committee, says it has been directed by the Presidency to oversee the supply and distribution of fuel across the country.
- Telephone subscribers have snapped up the few lines on offer from privately run Disc Communications in spite of a cost of 167,000 naira per line.
- A shortage of aviation fuel is imminent as production of Aviation Turbine Kerosine has been stalled by the non- availability of crude oil at northern Kaduna refinery.
- Federal government has told all civil servants who wish to take part in politics to resign or retire.
- United Nigeria Congress Party, the most successful in recent elections, has ruled out a merger with any other political party.
- The Delta Steel Company, shut since 1986, needs $60 million to refurbish its plant for production, the general manager says.
